newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Uganda Airlines starts service to new Congo.
newsitem.headline: Uganda Airlines starts service to new Congo.

text.p: Uganda Airlines operated its inaugural flight into the capital of Laurent Kabila's new Congo on Monday, underlining a growing alliance between the two neighbours.
Officials of both Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda said Kabila's takeover in the former Zaire in May would open up new opportunities for regional cooperation.

Uganda and Rwanda were among the key backers of Kabila's seven-month guerrilla campaign which began from the borders of the two states. Rebel forces entered Kinshasa in May, ending the 32-year rule of president Mobutu Sese Seko, whose government had frosty relations with Uganda.
In a speech before several guests at a Kinshasa hotel, Uganda Airlines general manager, Jack Turinawe, said his company would operate two flights a week into the Congo capital.

"Given the atmosphere that has been created by the liberation of this country we considered it most appropriate for us to be part of the process of furthering the regional development by facilitating easy movement of people, goods and ideas in our region and beyond," Turinawe said.
"Cooperation of Uganda airlines and Air Congo will be a key factor in rebuilding and strengthening our countries' economies," he said.
The interim general manager of Air Congo said the Congolese air company and Uganda airlines were to finalise three agreements in the next few days. He did not elaborate.
Air Congo is virtually bankrupt after years of mismanagement. Many of its staff have not been paid for more than two years.
